stories.title: Vienna Final — Alcaraz vs. de Minaur, H2H 6-0 Alcaraz as de Minaur Looks for First Win

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Alcaraz vs. de Minaur — Vienna final is underway. H2H: 6-0 Alcaraz. But de Minaur just beat Zverev coming back from 0-3 in the final tiebreak. The streak is real. The question is whether it crosses over today. #TennisFanrecap #ViennaOpen

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Vienna final: Alcaraz bidding for his 28th career title and 4th of 2026. De Minaur stunned the world No. 1 to get here. One of the better finals of the autumn swing — follow @TennisFanrecap for results. #TennisFanrecap #ViennaOpen

facebook.image_caption: Vienna final — Alcaraz vs. de Minaur. The H2H is 6-0. The momentum belongs to de Minaur. One of them goes home with the trophy. Which way do you think it goes?

article.headline: Vienna Final: Alcaraz vs. de Minaur — Can de Minaur Crack a 6-0 Head-to-Head Deficit?

stories.title: Basel Final — Lehecka vs. Vacherot Clash in All-Surprise Sunday

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: The Basel final nobody predicted: Vacherot vs. Lehečká. Vacherot (Monaco, ranked No. 31) beat Fritz. Lehečká saved a match point to beat Struff. H2H: 1-1. Tennis remains gloriously unpredictable. #TennisFanrecap #SwissIndoors

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Also today — Vacherot draws Djokovic in Paris R1 on Monday. Win Basel, fly to Paris, play the all-time great who's never beaten you. No days off in November. #TennisFanrecap #ParisMasters

facebook.image_caption: Basel final: Vacherot vs. Lehečká. The first player from Monaco to reach this final. A Czech comeback specialist who saved match point to get here. Tennis makes no promises — and that is exactly why we love it.

article.headline: Basel Final: Lehecka vs. Vacherot — A Surprise Sunday in Switzerland

stories.title: Paris Masters Draw: Djokovic Faces Vacherot R1, Needs Semifinal to Qualify for Turin

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text: Paris Masters draw is set. Zverev (No. 1), Alcaraz (No. 2), Shelton (No. 3), Medvedev (No. 4). Djokovic seeded 10th — opens against Vacherot, who beat him at Shanghai last year. Paris starts Monday. One week, 1,000 points. #TennisFanrecap #ParisMasters

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text: Djokovic needs a semifinal in Paris just to qualify for Turin. His R1 opponent: Vacherot, who has never lost to him. His R3 if he gets there: de Minaur. His QF: probably Zverev. That is not a soft draw. #TennisFanrecap #ParisMasters

facebook.image_caption: Paris Masters 2026 draw is here. Djokovic needs a semifinal to qualify for the ATP Finals. His first opponent: the one player who has beaten him on tour lately. No easy path. No guarantees. Just Paris in November.

article.headline: Paris Masters Draw: Djokovic Opens Against Vacherot — and Needs a Semifinal to Reach Turin

stories.title: ATP Race to Turin — De Minaur Holds Ninth, Fritz Fading, Three Spots Still Open

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Race to Turin update: Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton, Medvedev are in. De Minaur is 9th — one point ahead of Jodar. Fritz fading. Djokovic, Fils, Tiafoe all chasing. Paris is the last chance, worth 1,000 points to the winner. #TennisFanrecap #ATPFinals

facebook.image_caption: Race to Turin, today's snapshot: 4 in, 4 spots left, de Minaur 9th by literally one point. Paris starts Monday. One tournament, everything on the line.

article.headline: ATP Race to Turin: Four Spots Left, De Minaur Leads by One Point as Paris Begins

stories.title: WTA Finals Begin in One Week — Eight Players Set, Draw Ceremony Wednesday

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: 7 days until the WTA Finals at Indian Wells. Draw ceremony: Wednesday. Players: Rybakina, Sabalenka, Andreeva, Pegula, Gauff, Svitolina, Noskova, Muchová. Swiatek is out. No defending champion has looked more beatable in years. #TennisFanrecap #WTAFinals

facebook.image_caption: WTA Finals week is here — seven days until play starts at Indian Wells. Eight players. No Swiatek. No clear favorite. The most open field in years. Which player are you backing?

article.headline: WTA Finals Preview: No Swiatek, Eight Players, and the Most Open Field in Years
